dharana.rendering: Seated on a soft seat on the buttocks alone, with hands and feet left without support, by remaining in that position the mind becomes supreme and full.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: seated on a soft cushion, resting on only one buttock (sphijā ekena), hands and feet without any support, in a very relaxed way; agitation and dullness fall away and the mind reaches equilibrium (sattva). Wallis: 'with only the buttocks touching it and the hands and feet suspended in the air'.

dharana.instruction: Observe only: read and understand this classical description. It is not practised in class. For practice, use Door 059.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition, with one exception that belongs to the verse: verse 78 itself describes the position (a soft seat, the buttocks alone, hands and feet without support). That position is recorded in the method as part of the classical description, without any posture name. Everything else about the seat is a convenience, not part of the technique.

points: contact with the soft seat (the buttocks only)
geometry.summary: Not a body shape to copy. The classical map is a single area of contact with a soft seat and everything else unsupported. Drawn faint: studied, not drilled.
geometry.svg_hint: a faint outline touching a cushion at one point only, drawn faint to signal observe-only
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Unsupported (described)
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: with almost no support, the mind is pictured finding its own fullness. A picture to understand, not an exercise. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Study the verse; let the body rest fully supported while you do
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: Understanding the verse: the feeling of being unsupported can steady and fill the mind
attention.secondary: If sitting with anything, only the supported practice of Door 059

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Seated on a soft seat on the buttocks alone, with hands and feet left without support, by remaining in that position the mind becomes supreme and full.
adiyogi.method_summary: Classical method: sitting on a soft seat on the buttocks alone, with hands and feet held without support, and remaining so, the mind becomes supreme and full. Observe-only in this school: read and understand it. For practice, use Door 059 (contemplating the body as unsupported while fully supported).

honesty.disclosure: Door 055 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 55 (verse 78) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 055 is dharana 55, verse 78. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.

historical/observe_only: The technique is itself a specific unsupported body position (sitting on the buttocks with hands and feet held off any support). This school does not teach body positions as dharanas, and the unsupported balance can strain the back and hips or cause a fall. Taught as text to understand, not as a class drill.
Wallis's concordance heading for verse 78 is a posture name; it is withheld in this record under the school's no-posture-names rule.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. The unsupported balance is not taught. Anyone with back, hip or abdominal problems, or balance difficulties, should not attempt it. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
safety.observe_only_note: Observe-only. Holding hands and feet off the ground while balancing on a soft seat can strain the lower back, hips and abdomen and risks tipping over. For a related practice of feeling unsupported, use Door 059.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 055: sitting unsupported on a soft seat. Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 55, verse 78. This door is observe-only.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make, and no drill. Sit fully supported while we read. Its classical map is one point of contact and everything else unsupported.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Let the body rest completely. Eyes open, reading or resting softly. Attention on understanding, not on doing.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Natural breath only. Nothing to practise with the breath here. No forced hold.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Hold the idea only: the sense of being unsupported can steady the mind. For practice, Door 059 does this while fully supported.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: a mind finding fullness without props. A metaphor, not medicine.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 78: describes sitting on a soft seat on the buttocks alone, hands and feet unsupported, and the mind becoming full. Observe-only here. For practice, use Door 059.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Close the text. Take a normal breath. Look around the room and move on when ready.
